name: Adult-use
short: Legal, non-medical cannabis for adults, usually 21 and over in the US; the industry's preferred term for recreational cannabis.
definition: Adult-use is the term regulators and businesses use for cannabis sold to adults without a medical recommendation, what many people call recreational cannabis. In US states the minimum age is typically 21; in Canada it ranges from 18 to 21 depending on the province, and in Germany 18. Adult-use programs usually license separate or combined categories of growers, manufacturers and stores, and apply excise and sales taxes higher than those for medical cannabis.

As of early 2026, 24 states and Washington, D.C. had adult-use laws, according to congressional researchers. Federally, adult-use marijuana is still in Schedule I. The April 2026 rescheduling order covered only state-licensed medical marijuana, so adult-use businesses remain subject to the Section 280E tax penalty and cannot obtain the new DEA registrations.

That split matters for companies. Many states have merged medical and adult-use sales in the same stores, and how the DEA will treat businesses serving both markets has been a major open question. The distinction between adult-use and medical operations, once mostly a state tax issue, is likely to shape corporate structures, supply chains and tax filings until any broader federal change.
example: The company's adult-use stores remain subject to 280E while its medical-only stores now qualify for deductions.
